content.thinking: I need to understand how the activity service maps events to the audit log.

`archiveMember` sets a member's status to "suspended" while archiving them.

Removed members must not be found by `findMemberById`. Suspend and reinstate should throw NotFoundError for removed members.

`findMemberById` must distinguish removed members from suspended ones. A removed member has both status "suspended" and `archivedAt` set, while a live suspended member only has status "suspended". The lookup should filter out archived records.

`archiveMember` must keep its existing status logic. `countActiveMembers` should only count members with status "active".

I need to understand usage repository recompute, issue assignment, mentions, digest, org listing for a user, actor resolution, and error structure.

I need to examine TenantScopeError and Forbidden patterns for self-removal. I will review existing member service tests for last owner, self removal, and outranking scenarios. I also need to clarify that equal rank is permitted and only outranking ranks are blocked.

I need to examine `listOrgsForUser` and notification recipients to understand how notifications are created. This will let me skip suspended members.

NotFoundError should be thrown directly from `_support.ts` as specified. MemberSuspendedError needs to be wired into `toAppError` so it maps to a 409 conflict response.

The new member.suspended and member.reinstated actions must be added to the ActivityAction type, Zod schema, UI labels, activity service listeners, and TaskflowEventMap. I should also check if scripts/manifest needs updates.
ACTIVITY_LABELS is a strict Record mapping ActivityAction to string. Every new action requires a matching label or TypeScript will fail.

I need to determine how to check if a member is suspended versus removed.

A member is suspended only if status is "suspended" and archivedAt is null. Removed members have both fields set, so they are not suspended. The suspend and reinstate endpoints must reject archived members with NotFoundError. Missing members also return NotFoundError. Tenant scope errors apply when the orgId is outside the actor's organization.

The actor must have `member:remove` permission on the target member. Self-removal is refused, and I will throw a plain `Error` with a clear message since the spec does not define a specific error class.

The outrank rule blocks suspension or reinstatement when the target member's role is higher than the actor's. The actor must have at least the target's rank to proceed.

Equal roles are permitted for suspension or reinstatement. The last-owner guard must count only owners who are not suspended.

Invited owners also count toward the last-owner guard. The rule only excludes suspended members, not invited ones.

The `assertLastOwnerRetained` function should be reused for suspension and reinstatement. It currently requires a `nextRole` parameter, but suspension only changes status without altering the role. Since it is exported and only called by member-service, its signature can be adjusted to handle this case.

I will keep the existing `assertLastOwnerRetained` signature unchanged. The status filter will be added internally instead. This prevents demoting the last active owner when another owner is suspended, because the remaining owners count excludes suspended members.

Suspending a non-owner is safe because the function exits early when the member is not an owner. Reinstating a member does not reduce the count of active owners, so it requires no last-owner guard.

The idempotency rule for already-suspended members must run after the guards. If a member is already suspended, the endpoint returns unchanged and publishes nothing. The same applies to reinstating an active member. The check order matters because it must happen before any other logic.

Suspending an already-suspended member who is the last owner must return unchanged. The idempotency rule takes precedence over the last-owner guard in this case. Returning nothing is correct even if the workspace currently has zero active owners.

The self-suspend guard must run even when the member is already suspended. A suspended actor cannot be resolved, so this case is unlikely in practice, but tests may construct one manually. The spec treats self and rank checks as separate rules that always execute, and any refusal changes nothing.

The exact check order is now set: scope, existence, and permission first; then self and rank checks; then the last-owner guard only when the operation would actually change state; finally idempotency. Rank and self checks always run even if the member is already in the target status.

The rank and self checks must run even when the member is already in the target state. This prevents an admin from succeeding at suspending an owner who is already suspended.

Reinstating a suspended member returns it to active status and publishes an event. Reinstating an already-active member returns unchanged with no event.

Archived members must be treated as not found. The suspend endpoint should check `member.archivedAt !== null` and throw `NotFoundError` before any other logic.

The endpoint must validate tenant scope before looking up the member. If the actor belongs to a different organization, `assertOrgScope` throws `TenantScopeError` before any database query. The self-check compares user IDs directly.

The rank check compares ROLE_RANK values for the target member and the actor. A generic Error with a clear message will be thrown for both self-suspension and outrank failures, since the task requires named errors but the codebase does not define specific ones.

The last-owner refusal will reuse the existing Error message from `assertLastOwnerRetained`. Self and rank refusals may use `PermissionDeniedError` instead of a generic Error, since they are authorization checks in the same spirit as `assertCan`.

The rank check will mirror the existing `updateMemberRole` pattern, throwing a descriptive `Error` when the actor outranks the target. Platform staff are already permitted by `assertCan`, so they bypass the rank guard.

Staff will not bypass the rank or self checks. The specification does not grant them special suspension privileges.

The repository needs a new `setMemberStatus` method that accepts an organization ID, member ID, and either "suspended" or "active".

Seat counts must exclude suspended members from the active total.

Suspended members retain their seat. The active member count and usage rollup must include suspended members, but still exclude archived ones. Invited members remain excluded from both.

Suspended members are counted in active totals because the query filters for status "active" or "suspended" while excluding archived records. Archived members remain excluded from counts. Seat counts do not change on suspend or reinstate. Usage listeners only fire on joined and removed events.

createIssue passes input.assigneeId to insertIssue.

Suspended assignees must be rejected in createIssue and assignIssue. The error should only fire for existing suspended members, not null or unknown users. Un-assigning and assigning active members remain unchanged.

Removed members are not suspended, so assigning to them should remain allowed. The lookup will use findMember, which filters archived records and returns null for removed members while still surfacing suspended live members.

The suspended check runs before the write in both createIssue and assignIssue. Unassigning skips it entirely. Re-assigning an issue to a suspended member who is already assigned also throws.

updateIssue cannot set an assignee, so it needs no change.

Notifications must also exclude suspended members. The best place to block them is inside notify(), which covers both event fan-out and direct calls. Suspended recipients in the target organization should be filtered out there.

The daily digest must also exclude suspended members. listDigestRecipients or the job loop should skip them. Existing unread notifications remain untouched while suspended, but they will be digested once reinstated within the window.

Filtering suspended recipients will happen in listDigestRecipients and buildDigest as defense in depth. The digest service does not need to import the member repository.

listDigestRecipients will fetch digest subscribers and filter out any user whose member record is suspended or missing. This also excludes removed members, since findMember returns null for them.

Digest filtering should only exclude suspended members. Removed members must remain eligible for digests to avoid changing their existing behavior.

notify() will skip suspended recipients by checking member status inside the loop. Removed members still receive notifications because findMember returns null for them, preserving existing behavior.

Mentions must also exclude suspended members. The resolveMentions function will filter out suspended members before resolving handles, and client-supplied user IDs will be dropped so they never appear in stored comments or mention notifications.

The mention filter drops both suspended handles and client-supplied IDs. Suspended users will not receive mention notifications. They may still appear as assignee or author in comment fan-out, but the notify() filter blocks those notifications too.

The assignee picker already supports suspended members.

Domain events, activity schema, comment service mentions, and notification tests need review for exhaustive coverage. Member-service header comments must be preserved. The audit service needs member.suspended and member.reinstated listeners modeled after member.role_changed.

The audit record() function already reads actorId from the event payload. The suspendMember method should emit the event and let the activity listener record the audit row, following the existing member.role_changed pattern.

Considering Drizzle `inArray` or `or` for the status filter.

Usage-repository needs `or` or `inArray` from drizzle-orm. Checking if webhook events enumerate all types. The org switcher should exclude suspended members, but adding `status === "active"` would also exclude invited members. Need to verify whether invited members exist in the members table.

Invitations live in a separate table, so invited members are rare. The org switcher should exclude only suspended members using `ne(members.status, "suspended")` rather than filtering for active status alone. `switchActiveOrg` already rejects non-active members.
The member list already shows status.

Rank and self checks must run before the idempotency guard. This prevents a no-op from succeeding when the caller outranks the target or is acting on themselves. Viewers without member:remove permission will fail the permission assertion.

Rank checks apply to all callers, including platform staff. Staff bypasses do not override the outrank rule. Owners cannot suspend themselves.

countActiveMembers now counts suspended members, but existing tests still pass because fixtures contain only active members. The jobs test for usage.seatsUsed also remains correct after recompute.

Idempotent suspension of an already suspended owner returns early and avoids throwing on a no-op. Self and rank checks run inside loadGovernedMember before any idempotent return, so admins cannot bypass suspension.

Archived members are still found by ID but throw NotFound when checked for archivedAt. The archiveMember function sets both suspended and archived status.

Reinstating an invited member activates them. The spec only covers active reinstatement as a no-op, so invited members are not explicitly handled.

Reinstating should only apply when a member's status is suspended. Active and invited members must remain unchanged. The operation should publish an event only when it actually transitions a suspended member back to active.

The spec confirms that reinstating an active member returns unchanged and publishes nothing. The same applies to any non-suspended status. Suspending should only apply when the status is active; invited members must remain unchanged.

The last-owner bug is resolved by excluding suspended owners from the remaining set. The status filter already handles this correctly.

Removing a suspended owner is blocked when no active owners remain. This prevents the workspace from becoming ownerless.

findMemberById filters by orgId, so archived members from other organizations are not returned. TenantScopeError is thrown before the lookup when the actor's organization differs.
